correctness.rationale: The proof reduces arbitrary polynomial fields on the circle to (R−1)G, derives the normalized phase-adjoint identity s=−ωh′/2−kh, and applies the leading positive Fourier coefficient to prove deg G≥m+1. It separately handles constant h and shows any minimal realization has constant normal linearization. The explicit polynomial constructor has globally logistic radius, exact phase sensitivity and prescribed Floquet exponent. SymPy checks from the complete standalone source pass on the 2023 degree-seven example and eight additional rational harmonic profiles; the universal inequality follows analytically, not from testing. An independent exact 30-coefficient linear-system check for the published m=4 case shows coefficient-matrix rank 18 and augmented rank 19, excluding every polynomial competitor of degree ≤6 under the target adjoint.

value.rationale: High-harmonic oscillator phase-response design demands a principled minimum polynomial complexity, not only numerical feasibility. The theorem gives a sharp uniform answer m+3 against all polynomial competitors, proves optimal-degree radial damping rigidity, and attains arbitrary Floquet contraction with global attraction. The published degree-seven high-harmonic example directly motivates the sharp natural invariant.
